claims.text: 3348(g)(3) still defines 'special access program' by reference to 'Executive Order 12356 (or any successor Executive order)' — an order revoked in 1995 by E.O. 12958 sec. 6.1(d), as the GPO 'References in Text' note states. The operative definition today runs through the successor chain to E.O. 13526.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3348 - Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
claims.text: 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(3) defines 'special access program' as 'any program that, under the authority of Executive Order 12356 (or any successor Executive order), is established by the head of a department or agency whom the President has designated in the Federal Register as an original "secret" or "top secret" classification authority that imposes "need-to-know" controls or access controls beyond those controls normally required ... for access to information classified as "confidential", "secret", or "top secret".'

claims.text: The section heading is 'Reports relating to certain special access programs and similar programs'. The word doing the work is 'certain': DoD, NNSA and the Intelligence Community are routed out of it by subsection (g)(2)(B) to their own regimes, and the DoD regime it routes to, 10 U.S.C. 119, is the one carrying a waiver.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3348 - Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
claims.text: 3348(e)(1): 'The head of a covered department or agency may waive any requirement under subsection (a), (b), or (c) that certain information be included in a report ... if the head of the department or agency determines that inclusion of that information in the report would adversely affect the national security. Any such waiver shall be made on a case-by-case basis.' (e)(2) requires the withheld information and the waiver justification to be provided 'to the congressional oversight committees' -- with no reduction to chairs and ranking members.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3348 - Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
claims.text: 3348(f): 'A special access program may not be initiated by a covered department or agency until-- (1) the congressional oversight committees are notified of the program; and (2) a period of 30 days elapses after such notification is received.'

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3348 - Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
claims.text: 50 U.S.C. 3348(e)(2): where the waiver is exercised, the agency head 'shall provide the information described in that subsection with respect to the special access program concerned, and the justification for the waiver, to the congressional oversight committees' - the full committees, not a chair and ranking member.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3348 - Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
claims.text: 3348(g)(1) defines 'congressional oversight committees' as congressional leadership and the authorizing and appropriations committees with jurisdiction or shared jurisdiction over the department or agency, plus the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (now Oversight and Accountability). This definition was ADDED by Pub. L. 115-390 sec. 103(3) in December 2018; before that the statute said only 'Congress'.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3348 - Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
claims.text: THE COVERAGE HOLE. 3348(g)(2)(B): the term 'covered department or agency' 'does not include-- (i) the Department of Defense (which is required to submit reports on special access programs under section 119 of title 10); (ii) the National Nuclear Security Administration (which is required to submit reports on special access programs under section 2426 of this title); or (iii) an agency in the Intelligence Community (as defined in section 3003(4) of this title).' The government-wide SAP reporting statute therefore reaches none of the three communities where a legacy recovery program would plausibly sit.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3348 - Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
claims.text: Any special access program run by DHS, DOE outside NNSA, NASA, Commerce, Justice or any other non-excluded agency is reportable by statute to the House Oversight Committee - which means House Oversight's UAP subpoenas and document demands rest on a statutory entitlement that has not been publicly invoked. Reasoning: 3348(g)(1)(C) names the committee and (g)(2) excludes only three categories of agency.

claims.sourceText: 32 CFR 117.3(b) read against 10 U.S.C. 119 and 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(3)
claims.text: Because ACCM is defined as the case where SAP controls are not required, an ACCM is outside the definition of 'special access program' in 10 U.S.C. 119 and 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(3), and therefore outside every SAP congressional reporting statute. Reasoning: all four reporting statutes are triggered by the term 'special access program', which ACCM expressly is not.

claims.nodeLabel: The four SAP reporting regimes and the seams between them
claims.text: Four statutes, each with a different addressee. DoD: 10 U.S.C. 119 (defense committees; annual 1 Mar; waiver in (e) collapsing to chairman + ranking member). NNSA: 50 U.S.C. 2426 (congressional defense committees; annual 1 Feb; identical waiver). All other non-IC agencies: 50 U.S.C. 3348 (congressional oversight committees; annual 1 Feb; waiver that does NOT reduce the audience). IC: 50 U.S.C. 3091a (intelligence committees + both Appropriations + the four congressional leaders; semiannual briefings; no waiver at all).

claims.nodeLabel: The four SAP reporting regimes and the seams between them
claims.sourceText: Comparison of 10 U.S.C. 119(e), 50 U.S.C. 2426(e), 50 U.S.C. 3348(e) and 50 U.S.C. 3091a
claims.text: Of the four regimes, only 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) and 50 U.S.C. 2426(e)(2) narrow the recipient of waived information to the chairman and ranking minority member; 50 U.S.C. 3348(e)(2) keeps the full oversight committees, and 50 U.S.C. 3091a has no waiver provision at all.

claims.nodeLabel: Waived unacknowledged special access program (waived USAP)
claims.text: The parallel non-DoD, non-IC statute 50 U.S.C. 3348(e) contains the same waiver test ('would adversely affect the national security', 'case-by-case basis') but a materially WEAKER carve-down: 3348(e)(2) still requires the information to go 'to the congressional oversight committees', not merely to chairs and ranking members. The eight-member floor is therefore unique to the DoD statute.
